subject: Observability partner runbook & commercial alignment - marketplace listings
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Amaya Soto <amaya.soto@datadog.com>, marketplace@grafana.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Observability partner runbook & commercial alignment - marketplace listings

Hi Amaya, Grafana team —

Thanks for taking this on with us. As we discussed at the summit, Redwood is aiming to formalize a compact partner runbook for observability marketplace listings and resell pathways that covers: onboarding checklist, security/compliance gates, commercial economics, and operational SLAs (support, escalation, instrumentation).

Goal for this thread: align on the minimal set of artifacts each side needs for a marketplace listing + a simple resell option (partner-managed SKU). Specifically:
- A short runbook we can publish internally and share with partners (onboarding, cert matrix, required docs).
- Agreed commercial tiers (referral, co-sell, reseller) and sample revenue share ranges.
- SLAs / escalation paths for telemetry pipelines and labeled incidents.
- A short pilot plan (2 customers) to validate cost and latency expectations.

Can we set a 60-minute working session next week to draft the runbook and assign owners? I’m proposing Thu 10/15 10:00am PT — if that works I’ll send a calendar invite and attach an early draft.

I attached a simple outline to get us started (redwood-observability-runbook-v1.pdf). Ben and Laura are looped for commercial & procurement inputs.

Thanks —
Markus Klein
Head of Alliances, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-observability-runbook-v1.pdf (application/pdf, 320KB)

From: Amaya Soto <amaya.soto@datadog.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: marketplace@grafana.com
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability partner runbook & commercial alignment - marketplace listings

Thanks Markus — excited to work this through.

Quick notes from Datadog side:
- We can support both a marketplace listing (first-party listing) and a partner-managed SKU, but the partner-managed model needs a simple reseller agreement that covers support boundaries and who owns the customer contract.
- Procurement will require SOC 2 Type II evidence and a short data flow diagram for any agent/collector that touches customer PII.
- For commercial: Datadog prefers referral (1st year payout) for early pilots and will consider co-sell for proven demand. Rough ranges: referral 10–20%, co-sell splits TBD per opportunity.

I’ve looped Marketplace on required metadata for listing (catalog tile length, logos, listing screenshots). We’d like to see a single-runbook PDF and a one-sheet partner data sheet to expedite approvals.

Available for Thu 10/15 10am PT. Please send invite.

—Amaya Soto
Partner Programs, Datadog
amaya.soto@datadog.com

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability partner runbook & commercial alignment - marketplace listings

Markus / Amaya —

Nice. I kicked off a quick partner econ sketch (attached: partner-econ-model.xlsx) to surface the main levers: list price, expected usage, referral fee %, co-sell uplift, and channel margin if we do a reseller SKU. A few pragmatic suggestions:
- For pilots keep referral at 15% for year 1, then review. Keeps procurement simple.
- For reseller SKUs, propose a fixed margin band (20–30%) with a quarterly reconciliation to cover support cost variances.
- Include a small technical support uplift (charged monthly) for partner-managed telemetry ingestion — this covers our costs for prefix/KV cache tuning and dedicated monitoring.

KPIs to include in the runbook: time-to-onboard (days), avg token latency delta during pilot, cost per 1k tokens, incidents per quarter. If we can agree on those, integrations & field marketing are straightforward.

I’ll be on the Thu working session.

—Ben Carter
Sr. Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachment: partner-econ-model.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 42KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, Amaya Soto <amaya.soto@datadog.com>
Date: Sat, 16 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability partner runbook & commercial alignment - marketplace listings

Folks —

A couple procurement/legal items to lock before we publish anything to a marketplace:
1) SOC 2 evidence + annual attestation (Datadog asked for this explicitly). We should include a short Q&A in the vendor profile that points to our SOC report location.
2) Data residency and retention bullets — customers will ask what telemetry we store, how long, and who can access the KV/cache. Add a short section in the runbook.
3) Marketplace terms: Grafana will want a catalog tile + logos + approved marketing language. Marketplace typically requires a legal contact and a PS contact for onboarding.
4) SLA note: we need a runbook appendix that states escalation path (Tier 1 partner support -> Redwood support -> Datadog/Grafana ops) and an SLA credit matrix for platform-impacting incidents.

I reviewed Markus’ draft and left a few inline comments in redwood-observability-runbook-v1.pdf. I recommend we lock the procurement checklist in the first week of the pilot so sales can start packaging offers.

Laura Bennett
Head of Field Ops, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Thanks all — great alignment so far. Recap + MAP below (short, actionable):

Mutual action plan (MAP):
- 10/20: Working session — Thu 10/20 10:00am PT (60m) to turn the draft runbook into a publishable doc. Owners: Markus (runbook lead), Amaya (Datadog listing metadata), Laura (procurement checklist), Ben (econ model).
- 10/27: Pilot launch readiness — confirm two pilot customers and sign-off on referral economics. Owner: Ben.
- 11/10: Marketplace listing submission (Grafana / Datadog), include SOC2 link and data residency bullets. Owner: Amaya / Grafana team.
- Ongoing: Track KPIs (onboard days, latency delta, incidents); monthly cadence first quarter. Owner: Sergio (ops metrics).

Attachments & links: I’ve attached the latest draft and Ben’s econ model. I’ll upload a clean runbook to Drive after the working session: https://drive.google.com/file/d/driveid-runbook

Next steps: I’ll send the calendar invite for Thu 10/20 and include a short agenda (draft review, econ table, procurement checklist). If anyone needs a different time, shout here.

Thanks again — this feels high impact and pragmatic.

—Markus Klein
Head of Alliances, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-observability-runbook-v1.pdf, partner-econ-model.xlsx
